name: Taikat
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog taik1255 cites only Voorhoeve 1975 and Donohue & Crowther 2005 (classification); no phonological description of Taikat located

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU. Entry 102 TAIKAT (Arso), p. 43; wordlist conventions p. 92.
sources.note: Checklist entry only (villages; sources Galis 1955, Cowan 1957b, Voorhoeve 1971, Laycock 1973). Wordlist conventions p. 92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'
sources.venue: Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31)

sources.note: Only 'six vowels /a e i o u ə/' (citing Foley 2018); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark & Melissa Crowther. 2005. Meeting in the middle: interaction in North-Central New Guinea. In A. Pawley et al. (eds), Papuan Pasts (Pacific Linguistics 572), 167-184. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Areal phonology of Skou/Serra Hills/One/AN languages; Border family represented only by Ningera (p. 181, 'not tonal'). Taikat is not described; it appears only in Ross's plant-name chapter (pp. 674-675). No Taikat stress statement.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages / Border Stock section 2.6.2.2.11, pp. 414-417, in S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: p. 417: 'The phonemic systems of Awyi and Taikat are practically identical; in Taikat the voiced stops do not seem to have prenasalized allophones; instead of a lateral l, there is a flapped r. There is possibly a uvular fricative h.' Nothing on stress; the stress remarks on pp. 418-419 concern Senagi and Pauwasi languages, not Taikat.
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38)

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. E. Dutton et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU. Section 2.3 Tami Stock, 2.3.3 Phonology pp. 62-64.
sources.note: Tentative Taikat phonology (lightly aspirated voiceless stops, no prenasalised voiced stops, [B]~[b], flapped r, f, s, possible uvular h; 6+ vowels; only single final consonants). No mention of stress, accent, pitch or tone for Taikat.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28)

sources.citation: Badan Bahasa, Peta Bahasa: 'Daikat (Taikat)' entry (idb 353) and Papua province list with separate 'Abrap' (idb 220, Kampung Sawanawa, Distrik Arso) and 'Marap' (Kampung Kwimi) entries.
sources.note: Location/dialectometry notes only; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Most recent survey covering the Border family; cited for the Taikat vowel inventory, may summarise prosody for Border languages.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide

sources.citation: Althur, Simin. 2002. Fonologi Bahasa Abrab. Jayapura: Universitas Cendrawasih / Proyek Penelitian Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia dan Daerah, Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Kanwil Depdikbud Propinsi Irian Jaya.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Taikat (Abrab/Abrap variety, Sawanawa village) in Glottolog; Indonesian 'Fonologi Bahasa X' reports of this series normally include a tekanan (stress) section.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1957. Prospects of a 'Papuan' comparative linguistics. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 113, 70-91 (Taikat = 'Arso' lexical data).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Earliest published Taikat ('Arso') data; comparative wordlist, unlikely to give a stress rule but might mark stress on forms.
sources.venue: Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 113

sources.citation: Galis, K. W. 1955. Talen en dialecten van Nederlands Nieuw-Guinea (names, wordlist, speaker numbers) and Cowan, H. K. J. 1957b (comparative treatment), as listed for Taikat in Voorhoeve 1975: 43.
